source.title: Critical initialisation in continuous approximations of binary neural networks
source.authors: G. Stamatescu; Federica Gerace; Carlo Lucibello; I. Fuss; L. White

record.file_problem: The full text is present. Some figure values are not recoverable from the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains differentiable surrogates for stochastic binary networks and examines how initialization and depth affect training performance. This tests initialization and trainability in a different network setting from V4.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports signal propagation theory and simulations of random networks. Those are not training-performance rows. The two training-performance plots report no exact numeric values in the text, so their values remain figure only.
record.test_reason: The study tests V4 in a new setting: continuous surrogates of stochastic binary networks. Its own MNIST training experiments vary initialization and depth and report that training performance follows the predicted correlation depth scale.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors recommend the deterministic surrogate for binary weights and neurons, and LRT for binary weights with continuous neurons. They advocate weight means near ±1 and bias variance approaching zero. Their training experiments provide qualitative support for initialization-dependent trainable depth, rather than demonstrating training at arbitrary depth.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains differentiable surrogates of stochastic binary networks, not the plain networks or initialization comparisons in V4's cited studies. Its experiments use MNIST and vary binary-weight-mean variance.
record.method_sensitivity: Training performance varies with depth and the variance of binary-weight means; the authors state that deeper networks require smaller learning rates and more training time.

fits_no_version.finding: The LRT surrogate with both binary weights and binary neurons has no critical initialization under the analyzed model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The existence of a signal-preserving critical initialization depends on the surrogate and whether neurons are binary or continuous.

record.problems: The plotted training-performance values are not stated numerically in the text. The experiments use an arbitrary fixed epoch count, and the authors say the theory does not specify how long critical-initialization effects persist. They describe the experimental validation as qualitative.
record.rows_left_out: The lower panels of Figure 2 compare trained deterministic and stochastic binary counterparts after 5 epochs. They are omitted because the reported comparison concerns Monte Carlo sample count and binary-network performance relative to the surrogate, rather than the initialization and trainable-depth effect captured by V4.

untested.parts: CIFAR-10/100 convolutional-network interpolation, including corrupted or random labels.
Spurious local minima and student overparameterization in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth degradation in batch-normalized convolutional networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts or the specified alternative recipes.

Orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, convolutional kernels, and training at 10,000 layers. The fixed ten-epoch measurements do not establish convergence times or trainability at arbitrary depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, catapult recovery, sharpness dynamics, and divergence.
Batch-normalization speed and learning-rate comparisons, including Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V4. Fixed training budgets and the need for smaller learning rates at greater depth qualify the strength of the evidence, but do not contradict V4. Signal-propagation simulations alone do not measure training performance. The binary-counterpart comparisons are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: The training experiments use MNIST and binary-network surrogates, not sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, corrupted labels, or random labels.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem or neuron-width comparison.
No comparison of plain networks with identity residual shortcuts.
The training experiments vary binary-weight-mean variance and depth in MNIST surrogates. They do not compare orthogonal with Gaussian initialization or test 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
No learning-rate stability threshold or curvature dynamics are tested.
The training experiments explicitly omit batch normalization and do not compare normalization with Fixup.

relationships.condition: Deterministic and continuous-neuron LRT surrogates on half of MNIST, depths below 70, zero initial biases, and ten training epochs.
relationships.reason: R1 and R2 show initialization-dependent training performance that the authors explicitly report follows the correlation depth scale, with greater trainable depth toward critical initialization. Evidence is qualitative; exact accuracies are unavailable.
relationships.display_finding: Training performance followed the correlation depth scale, with greater trainable depth toward critical initialization.
